title: One patient, seven handoffs
idea: Sketch a synthetic patient journey and ask leaders which handoff their team repeats most.

title: The hidden cost of searching
idea: Describe the time spent finding a result across teams as a question to measure, without inventing a savings figure.

title: When two reports disagree
idea: Pose a board-meeting scenario where finance and clinical reports disagree and show three questions to ask.

title: The duplicate-entry trail
idea: Phone-filmed desk sketch follows one fictional lab order copied between reception, clinician, and billing.

title: Three calls for one result
idea: Founder acts out three routine calls needed to locate one synthetic result and asks what happens locally.

title: The spreadsheet behind the dashboard
idea: Show a blank synthetic spreadsheet and the questions a CEO should ask about report preparation time.

title: How to map a patient handoff
idea: Step-by-step guide to drawing one patient's movement through departments and marking repeat entry.

title: Why hospital reports disagree
idea: Explain differences in definitions, timing, missing data, and manual reconciliation without blaming one vendor.

title: What a delayed claim does and does not mean
idea: Distinguish rejected claim, delayed cash, missed legitimate charge, and unrecoverable revenue.

title: Patient-pathway friction worksheet
idea: One-page template to count handoffs, repeat entries, wait points, owners, and a starting baseline.

title: Five-minute handoff check
idea: Self-assessment that returns the first pathway worth discussing, not a made-up hospital score.

title: Founder-built scope trace
idea: Use the public founder-authored Medplum case-study context as product-history evidence, clearly not a customer outcome endorsement.

title: Synthetic handoff before/after
idea: Show a clearly labeled synthetic workflow comparison to prove the method is inspectable, not that savings occurred.

title: Where the work repeats
idea: Send the worksheet with one question about the hospital's last repeated handoff; no generic AI pitch.

title: A report you had to rebuild
idea: Invite a leader to identify one report that requires manual reconciliation and the person who prepares it.

title: Hospital-operator discussion prompt
idea: In an appropriate Georgian hospital-leadership forum, ask how teams map a handoff; participate only where welcome.

title: Clinical-operations partner note
idea: Offer the neutral worksheet to a clinical operations association or trusted professional contact for feedback.

title: Fix a screen or fix the pathway?
idea: Compare three practical options: current-vendor change, narrow tool, or shared operating system for the same handoff.

title: What parallel evaluation actually requires
idea: Name the hospital owner, data permission, baseline, and staff time behind an honest two-week evaluation.

title: AI assists; clinicians decide
idea: Explain a reviewed draft or flag in a fictional pathway and show where the clinical decision stays human.

title: Three options on one whiteboard
idea: Founder draws status quo, point solution, and operating-system path with honest change effort for each.

title: What happens in 25 minutes
idea: Preview the founder-led pathway demo: buyer names a handoff, founder maps it, team picks a first measure.

title: A result becomes a task
idea: Synthetic screen-recorded example shows a result routed to a named reviewer, with no patient data.

title: How to evaluate hospital software without a risky cutover
idea: Guide to pathway scope, authorized data, parallel workload, success criteria, reconciliation, and sign-off.

title: Hospital OS versus overlay versus current vendor change
idea: Decision guide for when each option is appropriate, including cases where replacement is not justified.

title: What FHIR R4 changes in hospital work
idea: Plain-language explanation of a shared data structure and the interface work still required.

title: Parallel-evaluation readiness checklist
idea: Checklist for named owners, agreed pathway, data permissions, baseline, IT review, and stop criteria.

title: Three-option decision worksheet
idea: Template comparing incumbent fix, narrow add-on, and MediMind against burden, risk, cost, and scope.

title: Documented domain map
idea: Publish the 25-domain scope as an internal product map with clear deployed, accepted, and pending fields after verification.

title: Live-pathway evidence template
idea: Show the exact baseline and after fields a customer-approved case study would need; label outcome cells pending.

title: The change-risk question
idea: Explain what a parallel comparison can answer and ask which transition failure the hospital fears most.

title: The current-vendor alternative
idea: Invite the buyer to compare a current-vendor fix with a connected pathway using the same criteria.

title: Peer discussion on evaluation design
idea: Ask consenting hospital operators what evidence they require before changing a core workflow.

title: IT and clinical review session
idea: Offer an educational walk-through of data, safety, and cutover questions with no sales claims.

title: What your 25-minute demo will settle
idea: List the three outputs: first pathway map, first metric, and evaluation readiness decision.

title: Match price, define total cost
idea: Describe early-partner software-price match and the need to itemize transition and third-party costs.

title: The honest go/no-go test
idea: Show how leadership can decide after staff compare one pathway and its extra work or risk.

title: Demo in sixty seconds
idea: Founder shows synthetic map, shared task, and comparison worksheet as the demo preview.

title: Parallel beside current work
idea: Draw existing and proposed pathways side by side and explain readiness, workload, and sign-off.

title: Who should join the first call?
idea: Name CEO or operator plus optional clinical/operations and IT counterparts, depending on decision stage.

title: Questions to ask before a hospital OS demo
idea: Give buyers questions about scope, human review, data rights, deployment proof, and total cost.

title: What happens after a parallel evaluation
idea: Explain measured review, reconciliation, approval, and staged rollout; no automatic production switch.

title: What current-software price match should include
idea: Explain the questions a hospital should settle about eligible spend, term, development, and total cost.

title: Pathway demo preparation card
idea: One-page card for an executive to bring a recent incident, current workaround, owner, and desired measure.

title: Evaluation decision sheet
idea: Go/adjust/stop template that records baseline, staff burden, risk, cost, and sign-off owner.

title: Verified implementation timeline
idea: After authorization, publish dated scope, readiness, and acceptance milestones from a real customer without claiming broad outcomes.

title: Buyer-approved workflow result
idea: Reserve case study for a measured result and customer permission; until then show evidence fields as pending.

title: Your pathway before our demo
idea: Ask attendee for one recent handoff and offer the preparation card; do not request patient-identifying details.

title: What we will compare
idea: After demo, send a proposed baseline and evaluation scope with unresolved requirements visibly marked.

title: Private buying-committee walkthrough
idea: Convene named clinical, finance, operations, and IT evaluators around one pathway, by invitation.

title: Procurement questions session
idea: Offer a structured discussion of costs, responsibilities, support, and exit needs with the buying group.

title: First pathway, first baseline
idea: With permission, describe the method for recording a baseline after sign-up, without showing confidential data.

title: What staff should report in week one
idea: Explain how to capture repeat work, exceptions, and safety concerns during a controlled evaluation.

title: One improvement, then the next
idea: Show an anonymized learning loop: observe, prioritize, test, approve, measure; no unverified success claim.

title: How to log a handoff issue
idea: Phone walkthrough of an issue form with synthetic patient data and an owner for follow-up.

title: Five-minute pathway review
idea: Show how clinical and operations owners compare the agreed metric and exceptions each week.

title: How a testable change becomes approved
idea: Explain request, test, clinical/IT review, and production approval with a generic example.

title: Measuring repeat work without double counting
idea: Define staff time, task count, training burden, and why minutes do not automatically equal cash savings.

title: Running a safe pathway review
idea: Guide to issue ownership, clinical escalation, baseline comparison, and go/adjust/stop decisions.

title: Selecting the second pathway
idea: Criteria for choosing a next workflow after the first is accepted: frequency, burden, risk, and readiness.

title: First-pathway measurement sheet
idea: Customer worksheet for baseline, tasks, exceptions, staff burden, and sign-off.

title: Change-request decision card
idea: Template for request owner, test criteria, clinical impact, priority, and production approval.

title: Accepted-workflow log
idea: Internal customer-approved ledger of which pathway elements were accepted and which remain open.

title: Measured improvement record
idea: Record an actual agreed before/after comparison only after data quality and buyer sign-off; no public release by default.

title: Your first review agenda
idea: Send the clinical/operations owner a concise agenda for metric, exceptions, staff feedback, and next decision.

title: A request ready for test
idea: Tell the named owner what changed, where to test it, what remains unapproved, and how to respond.

title: Clinical-IT issue huddle
idea: Short private working session for clinicians and IT to resolve one observed pathway issue.

title: Cross-site learning exchange
idea: With a group customer, invite site owners to compare process lessons without patient details.

title: The buyer's permission comes first
idea: Explain what a responsible public hospital story needs: verified result, named scope, and permission.

title: A pathway another leader can inspect
idea: After approval, share a measured pathway story with method and limits rather than a sweeping transformation claim.

title: What we changed after feedback
idea: Publish a consented example of customer feedback becoming a tested product change, with dates verified.

title: Customer pathway walkthrough
idea: With customer approval, have staff explain a measured before/after task using non-identifying visuals.

title: What a reference actually verified
idea: Founder shows the evidence standard and a permissioned result; hold production until proof exists.

title: Why we chose the first pathway
idea: Customer-approved owner explains why the initial workflow was selected and what remains unsolved.

title: How to read a hospital software case study
idea: Teach readers to distinguish contracted sites, live sites, accepted workflow, and measured outcome.

title: From one hospital pathway to another
idea: Permissioned account of what transferred across sites and what required local redesign.

title: What changed in a claim handoff
idea: Only after verification, explain actual claim-process result and separate identified charges from collections.

title: Reference-story evidence checklist
idea: Template a hospital can use to evaluate any vendor story: baseline, denominator, site, dates, approval.

title: Peer evaluation guide
idea: Guide for hospital executives to ask a reference about transition burden, support, and continuing development.

title: Buyer-approved measured case study
idea: Publish only after customer permission and audited baseline, method, result, and limitations.

title: Reference conversation
idea: Offer a customer reference only after that customer's explicit agreement, with scope and availability confirmed.

title: Share the method, not a claim
idea: Ask a satisfied authorized customer whether they would review a draft factual pathway story.

title: A peer may have this problem
idea: After evidence and consent, offer a short forwardable note about the measured pathway and its limits.

title: Peer operator exchange
idea: With permission, convene an existing customer and one peer operator to discuss implementation lessons.

title: Hospital-association learning session
idea: Invite a permissioned customer to teach the pathway method; verify event and affiliation before promotion.
